newsitem.title: USA: Continental, pilots to seek mediation.
newsitem.headline: Continental, pilots to seek mediation.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc and its pilots agreed to seek federal mediation in contract negotiations, the pilots union said.

"As a result of developments at the bargaining table in Washington D.C. this week, the IACP and the company have jointly agreed to file for federal mediation for both Continental and Continental Express," the International Association of Continental Pilots (IACP) said in a recorded message for its members.
The union said it will provide additional details after Continental's shareholders' meeting on Friday. Continental representatives did not return calls seeking comment.
Negotiators representing the airline and its 5,000-member pilots union traded draft proposals to open the talks on April 2. The contract expires on June 30.
Continental, the nation's fifth-largest airline, said it hopes to have a new contract completed by July 1, but pilots say the deadline is less important than securing a good contract.

"We urge all of you not to be distracted by this turn of events at the bargaining table ... As we have said from the beginning of this process, it's the right contract that's important, not the signing date," the union said.
Negotiations on critical issue of pay and benefits began this week, the union said. The pilots are seeking a wage increase of up to 38 percent and improved benefits.
Tentative agreements have been reached on a number of issues such as seniority, training, physical examinations, union security and a new section on alcohol and drug testing, the union said.
